title: Overman v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: SJC adopted the officers' recommendation that complaint 92-9b be found not in order because Overman lacked standing as not subject to the jurisdiction of Eastern Carolina Presbytery (BCO 43-1; MSJC 6.2). It made no merits determination on the licensing of Arthur Peterson; the same basic issue was cross-referenced to a complaint by the Session of Antioch Presbyterian Church. The source header labels the disposition 'dismissed.'
first_summary: Overman complained to the General Assembly after the Eastern Carolina Presbytery licensed Arthur Peterson and denied his complaint. The SJC dismissed the complaint, holding that Overman lacked standing because he was not subject to the presbytery's jurisdiction. The merits of the licensing issue were left to a separate complaint by the Antioch Presbyterian Church session.
summary: Overman carried to the General Assembly his complaint that Eastern Carolina Presbytery improperly licensed Arthur Peterson, after the presbytery denied it. The SJC found the complaint not in order for lack of standing: Overman was not subject to the presbytery's jurisdiction (BCO 43-1; MSJC 6.2). It made no merits ruling; the same basic issue was noted as pending in a complaint by the Antioch Presbyterian Church session. The source header labels the disposition 'dismissed.'
